title: Equations of Circles
seo_title: Equation of a Circle Worksheet: Center, Radius, Completing the Square (Geometry) | 100 Questions
standard_text: Derive the equation of a circle of given center and radius using the Pythagorean Theorem; complete the square to find the center and radius of a circle given by an equation.
meta_desc: Free Geometry worksheet on equations of circles: standard form, center and radius, completing the square, diameters and points inside or outside. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: (x − h)² + (y − k)² = r²: center (h, k), radius r.
key_sub: Change the signs to read the center. Take the square root of the right side for the radius.
body_html:
How it works

A circle is every point at distance r from its center (h, k). The distance formula gives the standard form:

(x − h)² + (y − k)² = r²

The signs inside the parentheses are the opposite of the center: (x + 3)² means h = −3. The right side is r², not r.

If the equation is expanded, group the x-terms and the y-terms and complete the square for each, adding the same numbers to both sides.

Example

Find the center and radius of x² + 6x + y² − 4y = 12.

Add 9 and 4 to both sides

(x + 3)² + (y − 2)² = 25

Answer: Center (−3, 2), radius 5

Example

Write the circle with center (2, −1) through (5, 3).

r² = 3² + 4² = 25

Answer: (x − 2)² + (y + 1)² = 25

Common mistakes

  • Keeping the sign: (x − 4)² has center x = 4, not −4.
  • Writing r instead of r² on the right side.
  • Halving the right side to get the radius. Take the square root.
  • Completing the square on the left but not adding the same numbers to the right.

faq.q: What is the standard form of the equation of a circle?
faq.a: (x − h)² + (y − k)² = r², where (h, k) is the center and r is the radius.

faq.q: How do you find the center and radius from the equation?
faq.a: The center is (h, k), using the opposite signs of the numbers in the parentheses. The radius is the square root of the right side.

faq.q: How do you complete the square to find a circle's center?
faq.a: Group x-terms and y-terms, add (half the x-coefficient)² and (half the y-coefficient)² to both sides, then factor each group as a square.

faq.q: How do you write a circle's equation from the endpoints of a diameter?
faq.a: The center is the midpoint of the diameter and the radius is half the diameter's length.

items.q: A radio station at (1, −1) on a map grid reaches listeners up to 15 miles away. Which inequality describes the points it reaches?
items.e: Points within 15 miles of (1, −1) have a distance squared of at most 225: (x − 1)² + (y + 1)² ≤ 225.
